rv.q: More than four decades later this show exerts the same power on me it always has, maybe even more.
The songs are like a string of perfect pearls, polished to a bright glow by music director Marvin Laird.
Gypsy is often regarded as an indestructible musical; if that is true, Mendes's production is an unnecessary stress test.

Regardless, this production nonetheless demonstrates the great value to be found in being innovative while respecting an established work; that, if nothing else, makes this Gypsy one to remember, and one to wholeheartedly enjoy.

cn.t: Mendes delivers a stylish, well-crafted revival that respects the material, but critics find it lacks a truly galvanizing Rose. The production earns praise for its direction and musicality, yet falls short of greatness without a commanding central performance.

vs.sum: The Shubert Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, though some seats may require leaning forward for a full view. The sound quality is generally consistent and clear. While legroom is limited in some areas, the theater's historic charm and central location add to its appeal. Facilities are average, with typical lines at restrooms and concessions.

acc.note: 7 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No wheelchair-accessible restrooms (available across street).
